title: Hidden Ergodic Relaxation in the Quench Dynamics of a Bichromatic Mott Lattice
authors: Áttis V. M. Marino, Rhombik Roy, M. A. Caracanhas, N. D. Chavda, Antônio M. S. Macêdo, V. S. Bagnato, Robin P Sagar, B. Chakrabarti
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of strongly interacting bosons in a finite bichromatic Mott lattice following a sudden quench of the secondary lattice amplitude. The coefficient entropies and second Rényi entropy exhibit pronounced growth toward their Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) predictions from random-matrix theory, consistent with GOE-like statistical spreading in the employed multiconfigurational representation. In striking contrast, experimentally accessible observables, including the momentum distribution, fragmentation, and Glauber correlation functions, remain nearly unchanged throughout the evolution. For the sampled strong quenches, the coefficient entropies, second Rényi entropy, and the $N$-body coefficient spreading collapse onto a common relaxation trajectory that becomes largely independent of the perturbation strength. Our results reveal an emergent hidden ergodic relaxation beneath the persistent local Mott-like order. An effective embedded random-matrix model captures the qualitative crossover from restricted to extensive Hilbert-space spreading, providing an interpretive framework for the observed relaxation dynamics.
summary: This study examines how strongly interacting bosons in a Mott lattice evolve after a sudden quench. While local measurements suggest the system retains its insulating, Mott-like order, global entropy measures show clear, rapid relaxation consistent with random matrix theory (GOE). This reveals a hidden ergodic relaxation occurring in the wavefunction space, even when the system appears locally frozen.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics of strongly interacting bosons following a sudden quench in a bichromatic Mott lattice.
main_result: It reveals an emergent hidden ergodic relaxation in the global wavefunction statistics (entropy growth toward GOE), which occurs independently of the persistent, localized Mott-like order observed in experimentally accessible observables.
method: The dynamics are simulated using the MCTDHB method, analyzing both global Hilbert-space spreading measures (entropies) and local observables (momentum distribution, correlation functions).
model_or_system: The system consists of strongly interacting bosons confined in a finite one-dimensional bichromatic Mott lattice. The dynamics are initiated by quenching the secondary lattice potential.
key_observables: Coefficient Shannon entropy ($S_C$), second Rényi entropy ($S_2$), momentum distribution $n(k, t)$, and local two-body Glauber correlation function $g^{(2)}(0, 0; t)$.
important_parameters: Strong interaction regime, quench strength ($V_d$), and system size ($N=9$ bosons in $S=9$ sites).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the MCTDHB framework and assumes that the observed entropy growth characterizes the global relaxation process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the contrast between the slow evolution of local observables (Mott order persistence) and the rapid, GOE-like growth of global entropy measures ($S_C, S_2$) following the quench.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and quench protocol, presents diagnostics for both local (low-order) and global (entropy) observables, and then contrasts the results to argue for the existence of hidden ergodic relaxation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental question of whether global quantum chaos/relaxation manifests in measurable, low-order observables in strongly correlated quantum systems, which is central to understanding thermalization in quantum gases.

figures.caption: FIG. 2. Time evolution of the orbital entropy Sn(t) for dif- ferent quench amplitudes Vd. Strong quenches (Vd = 5, 6, 7) rapidly reach a stationary value, while weak quenches retain fluctuations, consistent with persistent Mott-like correlations at the orbital level.

FIG. 1. Dynamics of experimentally accessible observables following a sudden quench of the secondary quasiperiodic lat- tice for N = S = 9. (a) Momentum distribution n(k, t), (b) zero-momentum occupation n(k →0, t), (c) order parameter ∆(t), and (d) local two-body Glauber correlation g(2)(0, 0; t). Their weak temporal variations demonstrate the persistence of Mott-like order. Parameters are Vp = 10, Vd = 5, g0 = 0.5, and M = 10.

FIG. 3. Hilbert-space spreading after a sudden quench for N = S = 9. (a) Coefficient entropy SC(t), (b) second Rényi entropy S2(t), and (c) N-body coefficient spreading SN C (t). Weak quenches show restricted spreading, while strong quenches relax toward GOE values. Insets show the initial quadratic and intermediate linear regimes of S2(t). Pa- rameters: Vp = 10 and g0 = 0.5.

FIG. 4. Short-time fidelity F(t) after sudden quenches of the secondary quasiperiodic lattice for different quench am- plitudes Vd with N = S = 9. The faster decay for stronger quenches reflects enhanced many-body dephasing and rapid loss of memory of the initial state. Parameters are Vp = 10, g0 = 0.5.

FIG. 5. Numerical validation of the effective embedded random-matrix model. Dynamics of (a) the fidelity F(t), (b) the coefficient Shannon entropy SC(t), and (c) the second Rényi entropy S2(t) for different coupling strengths. Weak couplings exhibit limited dephasing and restricted Hilbert-space spreading, whereas strong couplings (λ = 5, 6, 7) show rapid entropy growth followed by saturation, indicating extensive configuration mixing and a stationary coefficient distribution.
